title: Continued rally before reversal: Q2 2026 Lithium Price Review
gist: Benchmark's Q2 2026 lithium review shows prices extending Q1's rally through April-May on a China export-tax-rebate cut and tight inventories, before reversing into a rumour- and policy-driven correction in June, with hydroxide, seaborne Asia, and Western prices all lagging the domestic Chinese carbonate move.

insights.claim: Lithium prices in Q2 2026 continued Q1's rally through April and early May before reversing into an uneven correction through June, as the market shifted from inventory- and feedstock-driven strength to rumour- and policy-sensitive selling.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Marks a clear mid-quarter inflection point — investors should treat the Q2 close as post-reversal, not peak, when modelling H2 lithium exposure.

insights.claim: Underlying lithium demand from EV and energy storage system (ESS) production was more stable through Q2 2026 than the volatility in spot pricing suggested.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Suggests the Q2 price swings were driven by trading and inventory dynamics rather than a genuine demand shock — real end-demand may be a steadier base case than spot price action implies.
insights.locator: "Underlying demand from EV and ESS production consistently proved more stable..."

themes.theme: China policy and carbonate price drivers

insights.claim: A reduction in China's export tax rebates took effect on 1 April 2026, after which domestic Chinese lithium carbonate prices rose on improving consumption and still-tight chemical inventories, with stockpiles moving downstream rather than accumulating with producers or traders.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A policy-driven rebate cut coinciding with a price rally and inventory drawdown to downstream levels signals genuine consumption pull, a bullish data point for near-term Chinese lithium demand.
insights.locator: "After a reduction in export tax rebates took effect on 1 April..."

insights.claim: Lithium hydroxide prices followed lithium carbonate's Q2 2026 rise but less aggressively.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The weaker hydroxide response versus carbonate points to relatively softer demand from the hydroxide-consuming, high-nickel cathode segment.

insights.claim: Outside China, seaborne Asia lithium prices lagged the domestic Chinese rally notably in Q2 2026, while European and North American prices were even slower to react as buyers approached procurement cautiously.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The regional lag implies ex-China lithium buyers were not chasing the rally — a signal that Western demand recovery is trailing China's, relevant for regional supply-chain positioning.
